Uncertainty Quantification for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models (2026)
edges.note: Where DDPM established the denoising-diffusion generative process, this paper treats flow matching as its continuous-time relative and asks how confident each generated action is rather than only how realistic it looks.

edges.source_label: DiT: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (Peebles 2023)
edges.target_label: Uncertainty Quantification for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models (2026)
edges.note: Where DiT showed a Transformer backbone can drive a diffusion model for sample quality, this paper adds calibrated uncertainty and an out-of-distribution detector on top of the flow-based action head.

edges.source_label: DiT: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (Peebles 2023)
edges.target_label: MetaWorld: Scaling Multi-Agent Video World Models from Single-view Video Data (2026)
edges.note: Where DiT denoises a single latent stream for one view, MetaWorld runs coupled streams tied with per-frame cross-attention so several views of one world stay geometrically consistent.

edges.target_label: MetaWorld: Scaling Multi-Agent Video World Models from Single-view Video Data (2026)
edges.note: MetaWorld runs the DDPM denoising process across coupled views and adds a monocular decomposition step, so multi-view training data can be recovered from single-view footage.

edges.source_label: DiT: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (Peebles 2023)
edges.target_label: Prisma-World: Camera-Controllable Multi-Agent Video World Model (2026)
edges.note: Where DiT denoises one view, Prisma-World puts all views in one full-attention sequence and injects relative camera geometry so the denoising is joint and geometry-aware.

edges.target_label: Prisma-World: Camera-Controllable Multi-Agent Video World Model (2026)
edges.note: Prisma-World makes the DDPM denoising geometry-aware and joint across views, trained on a synthetic dataset with exact camera labels.

edges.source_label: DiT: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (Peebles 2023)
edges.target_label: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation (2026)
edges.note: Where DiT applied a plain diffusion transformer to image latents, PointDiT applies the same denoiser to raw point-map patches for monocular geometry.

edges.target_label: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation (2026)
edges.note: Where DDPM defined the denoising diffusion objective for image synthesis, PointDiT reuses that objective to denoise 3D point maps directly in pixel space.

edges.target_label: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation (2026)
edges.note: Where ViT set the plain vision transformer backbone, PointDiT keeps it unchanged and conditions the denoiser on DINOv3 image tokens.

edges.target_label: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion: Tri-Mode Language Model (2026)
edges.note: Where DDPM applies denoising diffusion to continuous images, Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion trains the same objective jointly with autoregression so diffusion supplies parallel lookahead in a language model.

edges.target_label: Read It Back: Pretrained MLLMs Are Zero-Shot Reward Models for Text-to-Image Generation (2026)
edges.note: Where DDPM defines how to sample images, SpectraReward defines how to grade them during reinforcement-learning fine-tuning, using prompt-recovery likelihood rather than a trained scorer.

edges.target_label: Read It Back: Pretrained MLLMs Are Zero-Shot Reward Models for Text-to-Image Generation (2026)
edges.note: Where DiT sets the transformer-backbone diffusion class being fine-tuned, SpectraReward supplies a label-free reward from a frozen multimodal model's own image-conditioned prompt log-likelihood.

edges.target_label: Concurrent Image Understanding and Generation: Coupled Markov Jump Processes (2026)
edges.note: Where DDPM defines a one-way continuous denoising process with no channel to check its output against a reading of the image, this paper replaces continuous diffusion with coupled Markov jump processes and lets an understanding process steer and self-correct the generation process.

edges.source_label: DiT: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (Peebles 2023)
edges.target_label: Concurrent Image Understanding and Generation: Coupled Markov Jump Processes (2026)
edges.note: Where DiT keeps diffusion but swaps in a transformer backbone, this work keeps the transformer-style backbone but changes the underlying stochastic process to Markov jumps and couples two of them for joint understanding and generation.

edges.source_label: DiT: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (Peebles 2023)
edges.target_label: AlayaWorld: Interactive Long-Horizon World Modeling (2026)
edges.note: Where DiT replaced the U-Net with a transformer inside a single-image diffusion model, AlayaWorld scales that backbone to 15B and applies it to autoregressive video chunks with an explicit memory so frames stay consistent over long horizons.

edges.target_label: AlayaWorld: Interactive Long-Horizon World Modeling (2026)
edges.note: Where DDPM defined a fixed multi-step denoising process, AlayaWorld distills it to four steps per chunk so the model responds at interactive speed.

edges.target_label: Signal or Noise? Understanding Generative Models for Real-World Sensor Time Series (SensorGen, 2026)
edges.note: Where DDPM settled the generative-quality question for images and found diffusion the strongest family, SensorGen asks the same question for sensor time series and finds flow-matching, not diffusion, the strongest default, because sensor signals carry measurement noise and time-frequency structure that images do not.

edges.target_label: Signal or Noise? Understanding Generative Models for Real-World Sensor Time Series (SensorGen, 2026)
edges.note: Where Diffusion Beats GANs showed diffusion overtakes GANs on image fidelity, SensorGen re-runs that comparison for sensor signals under a single 14-setting protocol and finds the ranking does not transfer.

edges.source_label: Foundation Models for Biosignals: A Survey (Gu 2025)
edges.target_label: Signal or Noise? Understanding Generative Models for Real-World Sensor Time Series (SensorGen, 2026)
edges.note: Where Gu 2025 surveyed biosignal models and named the lack of systematic comparison as a gap, SensorGen fills it with a controlled study across 4 domains, 7 datasets, and 12 signal modalities.

edges.target_label: Signal or Noise? Understanding Generative Models for Real-World Sensor Time Series (SensorGen, 2026)
edges.note: Where Sensor2Text modeled sensor signals toward downstream use, SensorGen measures whether generated sensor signals improve downstream prediction, not only visual realism.
